Implement lexmem_memory.py + lexmem.py + config + tests, then go/no-go pilot on dil seed42 (new-task F1>=75, task-0 drop<=5).

Arm C (control, no memory): AA 38.9 ≈ B's 38.8 → bottleneck is 100% trunk drift, memory blameless. Arm D (lexmem_v3 = v2 + online EWC on plastic bucket, λ=1000) launched, commit 6d756ca. title: Fix empirical Fisher: per-sample gradient squaring (was batch-sum-then-square)
description: empirical_fisher_diagonal() in doccl/eval/fisher.py squared a batch-summed gradient (Σg)² instead of summing individually-squared per-sample gradients Σg². Because (Σg)²=Σg²+2Σ_{i<j}g_ig_j, the spurious cross-terms inflate highly-correlated parameter groups (the classifier head, whose per-token grads share logit weights) more than the backbone, overstating the head/backbone Fisher ratio by ~an order of magnitude. Fixed to one backward pass per document (within-doc tokens still summed). Unit-tested to match the textbook per-document reference exactly (atol 1e-6); corrected head/encoder ratio ~2.7x vs the old ~10x. Used by EWC/DocCL after_task (n_samples=200) and the pilot diagnosis.
close_reason: Fixed in doccl/eval/fisher.py: per-sample (per-document) gradient squaring; regression test test_empirical_fisher_is_mean_of_squared_per_sample_grads added; all Fisher tests pass.
